name: Natural Resources Defense Council
mission: The Natural Resources Defense Council's (NRDC) purpose is to safeguard the Earth: its people, its plants and animals and the natural systems on which all life depends. We work to restore the integrity of the elements that sustain life - air, land, and water - and to defend endangered natural places. We seek to establish sustainability and good stewardship of the Earth as central ethical imperatives of human society. NRDC affirms the integral place of human beings in the environment. We strive to protect nature in ways that advance the long-term welfare of present and future generations. We work to foster the fundamental right of all people to have a voice in decisions that affect their environment.
theoryOfChange: The Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) has a published 'Urban Solutions Strategic Plan' which explicitly includes a section titled 'OUR THEORY OF CHANGE' on page 24 of the document. This strategic plan outlines their approach to creating strong, just, and resilient communities by addressing climate change and inequality. The plan details how their strategies, tools, technical expertise, and on-site capacity aim to lead to the deployment of integrated, equitable, and replicable climate response strategies in urban areas.

strengths_deep_dive: NRDC demonstrates substantial operational scale and fiscal sustainability. In FY2024, the organization generated <cite id="[11]">$204,253,182 in total revenue</cite>, while directing a <cite id="[11]">77.5% program expense ratio</cite> toward its policy, legal, and environmental campaigns. This performance beats the general 75% sector benchmark for programmatic efficiency. Furthermore, NRDC maintains an exceptionally resilient financial position with <cite id="[1]">24.5 months of working capital in reserves</cite>, ensuring operations can withstand economic shocks or extended legal battles.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in <cite id="[10]">1970</cite>, the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) works to protect natural systems and public health through legal, scientific, and advocacy strategies. The organization addresses key environmental challenges, including climate change, toxic chemicals, and land conservation. In FY2024, NRDC reported <cite id="[11]">$204,253,182 in total revenue</cite>, supporting a broad array of advocacy campaigns across the United States and internationally. Financial filings show a <cite id="[11]">77.5% program expense ratio</cite>, which exceeds the standard 75% charity benchmark and demonstrates that a clear majority of funds directly support programmatic work. At the same time, NRDC maintains significant financial reserves, holding <cite id="[1]">24.5 months of working capital</cite> in working capital. Independent evaluations reflect high standard financial management, as shown by its <cite id="[1]">99/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite>. However, governance assessments highlight areas needing development, particularly regarding public board disclosures. While NRDC holds strong technical capabilities and global reach, its primary focus on environmental policy and advocacy offers an indirect, long-term approach to human welfare rather than immediate direct relief.
